chunks: Al-ʿAlāʾ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them, who said:
I asked him about the obligatory hady: if it is afflicted by a fracture or injury, may he sell it? And if he sells it, what should he do with its price?
He said: If he sells it, then he should give its price in charity and offer another sacrificial animal.

key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial animal designated for offering in hajj
key_terms.الْوَاجِبِ: that which is obligatory and must be fulfilled
key_terms.بِثَمَنِهِ: with its sale price or monetary value
key_terms.فَلْيَتَصَدَّقْ: then he should give in charity
key_terms.كَسْرٌ: a fracture or break affecting the animal

ai.seo_question: What should be done if an obligatory hady is injured or broken and then sold?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding an obligatory sacrificial animal in hajj when it becomes damaged before its intended use. If it is sold, its price must be given in charity, and another hady must be offered in its place.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3077 - Al-Ala narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (as), who said:
I asked him about a hady (obligatory sacrificial animal) that suffers a fracture or injury—can it be sold, and if sold, what should be done with its price?
Imam (as) replied: "If he sells it, he should give its price in charity and offer another sacrificial animal."
